title: Upgrading a kubeadm Cluster
summary: Upgrade one minor version at a time: kubeadm upgrade plan/apply, upgrade node, drain, kubelet packages, uncordon.

items: Upgrade **one minor version at a time** (e.g. 1.36.x → 1.37.x). Skipping minor versions is unsupported. Patch upgrades within a minor (1.37.x → 1.37.y) follow the same steps.
Order: **primary control plane node → other control plane nodes → worker nodes**. Control plane nodes go one at a time; workers one or a few at a time, keeping enough capacity for your workloads.
Swap must be disabled. Back up important components first; kubeadm upgrade doesn't touch your workloads.
Drain a node before a minor-version kubelet upgrade. Control plane nodes may be running CoreDNS or other critical Pods.
Match kubelet and kubeadm versions. An older kubelet is allowed if it is within the supported skew.
All containers restart after the upgrade because the container spec hash changes.
With pkgs.k8s.io, enable the package repository for the **target minor release** first. Find the latest patch with `sudo apt-cache madison kubeadm`.

sections.heading: First control plane node: plan and apply

blocks.text: Pick a control plane node that has `/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf`.

sudo apt-mark unhold kubeadm && \
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y kubeadm='<version>-*' && \
sudo apt-mark hold kubeadm

kubeadm version
sudo kubeadm upgrade plan
sudo kubeadm upgrade apply v<version>

items: `kubeadm upgrade plan` checks the cluster can be upgraded and lists target versions.

`kubeadm upgrade apply` checks health (API server reachable, all nodes Ready, control plane healthy), enforces version skew, upgrades the control plane static Pods (rolling back on failure), and applies new CoreDNS and kube-proxy manifests.
It also renews the certificates kubeadm manages on that node. Opt out with `--certificate-renewal=false`.
Then upgrade your CNI plugin by hand, following its own instructions.

blocks.text: On success you see `[upgrade/successful] SUCCESS!`. Only the control plane is done; next drain the node and upgrade its kubelet and kubectl. The node versions in `kubectl get nodes` update once the kubelets are upgraded.

items: Same steps as the first node, but use `kubeadm upgrade node` instead of `kubeadm upgrade apply`.
No need to run `kubeadm upgrade plan` or upgrade the CNI plugin again (if the CNI runs as a DaemonSet).
`kubeadm upgrade node` fetches the ClusterConfiguration from the cluster, upgrades the static Pod manifests and the node's kubelet configuration.
Since v1.28 the addons (CoreDNS, kube-proxy) are upgraded only after the **last** control plane instance is done, so upgrade them sequentially.

blocks.text:
kubectl drain <node-to-drain> --ignore-daemonsets

sudo apt-mark unhold kubelet kubectl && \
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y kubelet='<version>-*' kubectl='<version>-*' && \
sudo apt-mark hold kubelet kubectl

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart kubelet

kubectl uncordon <node-to-uncordon>

items: Check the kubelet came back with `systemctl status kubelet` or `journalctl -xeu kubelet`.
When every node is done, `kubectl get nodes` should show **Ready** and the new version.

blocks.text: Upgrade the control plane before the workers. Then, on each worker (one or a few at a time):

items: Upgrade the **kubeadm and kubectl** packages. kubectl must stay within one minor version of kube-apiserver.
Run `sudo kubeadm upgrade node`. On a worker this upgrades the local kubelet configuration.
From a control plane node: `kubectl drain <node-to-drain> --ignore-daemonsets`.
Upgrade the **kubelet** package, then `sudo systemctl daemon-reload` and `sudo systemctl restart kubelet`.
From a control plane node: `kubectl uncordon <node-to-uncordon>`.
`kubectl drain` evicts Pods so their containers terminate gracefully, and it respects your **PodDisruptionBudgets**.
DaemonSet Pods aren't evicted; the DaemonSet controller would just recreate them. Add `--ignore-daemonsets` so the drain can finish.
A drained node stays unschedulable. If it remains in the cluster, run `kubectl uncordon <node name>` afterwards so new Pods can land there.
Pods that tolerate the `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable` taint, or have `nodeName` set directly, can still run on a drained node.
Run one drain per node; drains for several nodes can run in parallel and still honour PDBs.
`kubeadm upgrade` is idempotent: just run it again. `sudo kubeadm upgrade apply --force` (same version) also recovers from a bad state.

Backups are written under `/etc/kubernetes/tmp`: `kubeadm-backup-etcd-<date>-<time>` (local etcd data; restore into `/var/lib/etcd`) and `kubeadm-backup-manifests-<date>-<time>` (restore into `/etc/kubernetes/manifests`).
These backups are not cleaned up automatically.
